rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (kp 4.5) scored 945.42 and iteration 8 (kp 5.0) scored 945.14. The two are within noise, so raising kp past 4.5 has stopped helping. Iteration 7 showed that lighter mass plus higher base_speed cost time and control effort, so I am not pursuing speed there. Across the last four iterations the score has sat near 941 to 945, which points to a local optimum in the current geometry and gain family. Per-track residuals: oval, s-bend and slalom all finish 20/20 with progress about 0.996. Line_loss_events are 0.25 to 0.5 per run (about 15 points each), completion time is 2.0 to 2.6 s, and slalom steering_oscillation (0.30) and control_effort (6.7 to 7.0) are the highest.

Change: keep the iteration 8 design (sensor_size 0.016, mass 0.6, body_length 0.11, base_speed 0.9, ki 0.05, line_loss last_direction) and raise kd from 1.0 to 1.2. The higher kp of 5.0 may be adding jitter. Extra derivative damping should cut slalom oscillation and control effort, and may also reduce the late corrections that cause line-loss events. Expected result: steering_oscillation down about 10 percent on slalom and s-bend, control_effort down, line_loss_events at or below 0.3, and completion held at 100 percent. Score change: small, about +0 to +10.

Hypotheses: H1, slalom line losses come from late corrections on sharp alternations, which more damping reduces. H2, if kd 1.2 adds noise-driven jitter on the oval (oscillation above about 0.25) with no line-loss gain, kd is past its useful range and the next step is to return to kd 1.0 and test ki 0.1 for drift. Measurements wanted: completion, completion_time, line_loss_events and max_error per track, plus steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness to check damping and noise margin.
